hints.content:
Usually, there are many different ways to divide polynomials. Here, we will use the method of splitting the quotient into multiple quotients:

$\dfrac{6x^2-4x-3}{x}=\dfrac{6x^2}{x}-\dfrac{4x}{x}-\dfrac{3}{x}$

Now let's try to cancel common factors in the resulting terms.

$\begin{align}
\dfrac{6x^2}{x}&=6x
\\\\
-\dfrac{4x}{x}&=-4
\end{align}$

$-\dfrac{3}{x}$ doesn't have common factors so it has to stay as it is.

In conclusion, this is the result of dividing the polynomials:

$6x-4-\dfrac{3}{x}$

[[☃ explanation 1]]

options.explanation:
We can perform the division using polynomial long division:

$\begin{array}{r}
6x-4
\\
x|\overline{6x^2-4x-3}
\\
\mathllap{-(}\underline{6x^2\phantom{-4x-3}\rlap )}
\\
{}-4x-3
\\
\mathllap{-(}\underline{{}-4x\phantom{-3}\rlap )}
\\
{}-3
\end{array}$

We get that the quotient is $6x-4$ and the remainder is $-3$, and therefore:

$\dfrac{6x^2-4x-3}{x}=6x-4-\dfrac{3}{x}$
